subject: SIG request: SDLC evidence for branch protection, CI keys, and rotation
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintegrity.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Fintegrity SOC Team <soc@fintegrity.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: Evidence request for SDLC controls

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As part of our SIG assessment we need sample artifacts showing how Redwood enforces secure software development practices. Specifically the assessor asked for:

1) Branch protection and PR enforcement: a screenshot or exported policy + an example merged PR that required 2 approvals and passed CI.
2) CI credential handling: evidence that service account keys used in pipelines are short-lived/ephemeral or rotated, plus the rotation schedule and where keys are stored.
3) Change management trace: an example of a change ticket -> PR -> deploy record chain (minimal PII) that demonstrates approval gating.

Could you send one consolidated packet (email + attachments) with the artifacts above? If there are quick links to the GitHub commit/PR and a short narrative mapping to SIG questions that would be ideal. Our deadline to include artifacts in the next assessor bundle is EOD next Thursday (2026-06-17).

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Senior Assessor, Fintegrity

--
attachment: request_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet listing desired items)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Fintegrity SOC Team <soc@fintegrity.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Evidence request for SDLC controls

Hi Alice,

Thanks — we can provide the artifacts. Attaching a short playbook and the rotation schedule now. Quick summary below and links to live artifacts:

- Branch protection: our main repo (github.com/redwood-inference/redwood) enforces branch protection on main and release/* with required status checks and 2 approvers. Example merged PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1248 (commit 8f3c2a9).
- CI credentials: we use ephemeral GCP service account tokens issued by our token-service, rotated every 6 hours. Persistent keys are not used in pipelines. Attached: ci-credential-rotation-schedule.csv and a small pipeline policy patch (ci_pipeline_policy.diff).
- Change management: example ticket SEC-4432 -> PR 1248 -> deploy record (artifact attached). The playbook maps these artifacts to SIG Workstream A3/A4.

I've attached: sdlc_playbook_v2.pdf, ci_pipeline_policy.diff, ci-credential-rotation-schedule.csv.

If the assessor needs screenshots of branch protection settings, I can export the repo protection JSON and a screenshot.

Priyom
Priyom Das
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

--
attachments: sdlc_playbook_v2.pdf, ci_pipeline_policy.diff, ci-credential-rotation-schedule.csv

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Evidence request for SDLC controls

Priyom — thanks for pulling this together. A couple of clarifications before we send the bundle:

- For the branch protection export, the assessor specifically asked to see the rule that blocks force-push and requires linear history. Can you include the protection JSON (not just a screenshot)?
- For CI keys, the assessor may ask for the token-service audit logs showing issuance and expiry for a sample run. We should redact any pipeline secrets but include request/expiry timestamps.
- Change management: include the Jira activity log snippet showing approvals on SEC-4432 (timestamps).

Action: Priyom — can you add the protection JSON, a single token-service audit log entry for PR-1248 run, and a JIRA export (audit) with the approval events?

I'll draft a one-page mapping to SIG control IDs after we have the items.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Security

--

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Quick notes from the runtime/CI side:

- Protection JSON: attached export (repo_protection_main.json) — shows required checks, dismiss stale approvals disabled, linear history required.
- Token-service log: sample entry (redacted) below. We issue short-lived OAuth tokens via our internal token-service; tokens include a unique request id and expiry. Example log (redacted):
  request_id=ts-20260607-91ac; service_account=ci-deploy; issued_at=2026-06-07T10:12:13Z; expires_at=2026-06-07T16:12:13Z; request_by=ci-runner-42
- CI pipeline: we run ephemeral auth flow — no persistent secrets in repo. The pipeline policy diff (ci_pipeline_policy.diff) includes a check that fails builds if a persistent key is detected.

I've uploaded the protection JSON and a sanitized token log to the secure drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sdlc-playbook-view (same as the playbook location).

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
